description: Fields from competitors/findings.jsonl that the contract has no place for, keyed by contract record_id / claim_id. Not read by the team validator or exporter.

luis:us_mercedes-F0063.statement: Reviewer notes the base E 350 is rated 25/33/28 mpg (city/highway/combined) versus 28/35/31 mpg for the 530i.

luis:us_mercedes-F0064.vfc_level2: Drive, driving dynamics and chassis, overall technology
luis:us_mercedes-F0064.statement: Reviewer judges both sedans refined and poised and calls the choice of driving feel a matter of taste.

luis:us_mercedes-F0065.statement: Reviewer favours the E-Class for buyers who want the newest tech, citing the Superscreen, Burmester 4D audio and an optional AI that learns routines.

luis:us_mercedes-F0066.statement: KBB's spec comparison shows the E-Class with less rear headroom (37.6 vs 39.1 in) and rear legroom (36.2 vs 37.0 in) than the 5 Series.

luis:us_mercedes-F0067.statement: Reviewer notes every E-Class variant gains a center airbag.

luis:us_mercedes-F0068.statement: Reviewer lists a KBB Fair Purchase Price of $58,000 for the E 350 versus $54,700 for the 530i, while calling overall pricing similar.

luis:us_mercedes-F0069.statement: Reviewer notes the E-Class powertrain warranty (4 years/50,000 miles) is shorter than the 5 Series' 6 years/70,000 miles.

luis:us_mercedes-F0178.statement: Reviewer praises a smooth, calm ride with a quiet electric powertrain.

luis:us_mercedes-F0179.statement: Reviewer states the low center of gravity gives agility and optional rear-wheel steering adds highway stability and a tight turning circle.

luis:us_mercedes-F0180.statement: Reviewer calls the EQE 350 4MATIC's roughly 6-second 0-60 mph time not brilliant and notes the i5 eDrive40 is 0.3 s quicker.

luis:us_mercedes-F0181.statement: Reviewer notes the EQE 350+ is rated at 308 miles of range versus 295 miles for the base i5 eDrive40.

luis:us_mercedes-F0182.statement: Reviewer lists as a con that the EQE 350 4MATIC and 500 4MATIC dropped to 267 miles of range, from 298.

luis:us_mercedes-F0183.statement: Reviewer states 10-80 % DC fast charging takes about 30 minutes, similar to the BMW i5.

luis:us_mercedes-F0184.statement: Reviewer describes the cabin as high-tech and luxurious, with comfortable seats and high-quality materials.

luis:us_mercedes-F0185.statement: Reviewer states the EQE's rear seat is roomier than the E-Class's, with no transmission tunnel.

luis:us_mercedes-F0186.statement: Reviewer notes the swooping roofline means bending more to get into the car.

luis:us_mercedes-F0187.statement: Reviewer calls the 11-cu-ft trunk small; the i5 offers 17.3 cu ft.

luis:us_mercedes-F0188.statement: Reviewer praises the full-width Hyperscreen and calls the EQE's tech superb.

luis:us_mercedes-F0189.statement: Reviewer notes KBB Fair Purchase Prices run about $4,850-5,550 below MSRP and expects above-average resale values.

luis:us_premium_others-F0097.statement: Reviewer states the 365-hp dual-motor Electrified G80 launches quickly in Sport mode.

luis:us_premium_others-F0098.statement: Reviewer states the estimated 282-mile range never caused range anxiety during the test.

luis:us_premium_others-F0099.statement: Reviewer lists the range below 300 miles as a con.

luis:us_premium_others-F0100.statement: Reviewer states the car is no sports sedan but handles mountain roads willingly, with great grip and above-average steering feel, and is quiet and smooth in Normal mode.

luis:us_premium_others-F0101.statement: Reviewer notes steering-wheel paddles adjust regenerative braking up to one-pedal driving.

luis:us_premium_others-F0102.statement: Reviewer warns that the round infotainment dial and the similar round gear-selector dial are easy to confuse.

luis:us_premium_others-F0103.statement: Reviewer states the heated and cooled front seats stay comfortable all day and include a leg and back massage function.

luis:us_premium_others-F0104.statement: Reviewer states rear legroom is snugger than in the gas G80.

luis:us_premium_others-F0105.statement: Reviewer states the trunk (10.8 cu ft) is slightly smaller than the gas G80's.

luis:us_premium_others-F0106.statement: Reviewer describes the cabin as posh and tech-heavy, with forged-wood trim and eco-friendly fabrics.

luis:us_premium_others-F0107.vfc_level2: Driver assistance, automated driving, overall technology
luis:us_premium_others-F0107.statement: Reviewer lists the many standard safety and assistance systems as a pro, including Highway Driving Assist, surround view and remote smart parking.

luis:us_premium_others-F0108.statement: Reviewer lists the single available trim as a con.

luis:us_premium_others-F0208.statement: Reviewer praises the smooth, comfort-oriented ride and would skip the F Sport Handling option with adaptive suspension.

luis:us_premium_others-F0209.statement: Reviewer lists the roomy cabin as a pro, with 39.2 in of rear legroom and angled rear seatbacks for headroom.

luis:us_premium_others-F0210.statement: Reviewer notes the rear seats do not split or fold.

luis:us_premium_others-F0211.statement: Reviewer calls the ES 300h's 215 hp not especially impressive.

luis:us_premium_others-F0212.statement: Reviewer highlights the ES 300h hybrid's 44 mpg combined rating.

luis:us_premium_others-F0213.statement: Reviewer calls the fuel economy of the gasoline-only ES 250 and ES 350 more tolerable than remarkable.

luis:us_premium_others-F0214.statement: Reviewer describes the cabin as calm and spacious with quality materials.

luis:us_premium_others-F0215.statement: Reviewer calls the ES relatively affordable for a luxury sedan, with strong resale value.

luis:us_premium_others-F0216.statement: Reviewer lists as a con that all-wheel drive is only available with the base engine.

luis:us_premium_others-F0332.statement: Reviewer lists tame performance as a con; even the quickest dual-motor ES 500e is tame compared with rivals.

luis:us_premium_others-F0333.statement: Reviewer finds the ES 350h hybrid noisy under hard acceleration, while the EVs are free of that engine noise.

luis:us_premium_others-F0334.statement: Reviewer notes the 244-hp ES 350h prioritizes efficiency, with Lexus estimating up to 46 mpg combined.

luis:us_premium_others-F0335.statement: Reviewer finds some interior materials odd, singling out the synthetic suede on the steering wheel, and suggests traditionalists may prefer real leather.

luis:us_premium_others-F0336.statement: Reviewer finds the front seats roomy even for tall drivers and the rear adult-friendly, with 40.7 in of rear legroom (1.5 in more than the outgoing ES).

luis:us_premium_others-F0337.statement: Reviewer praises the new infotainment system's crisper resolution and home button.

luis:us_premium_others-F0338.statement: Reviewer finds the tactile HVAC control bar below the screen easy to use.

luis:us_premium_others-F0339.statement: Reviewer finds the physical roller volume dial easy to use.

luis:us_premium_others-F0340.statement: Reviewer states the hybrid rides pleasantly.

luis:us_premium_others-F0341.statement: Reviewer calls the hybrid a uniquely good value with class-leading resale, noting the EV ES starts below $50,000 while the BMW i5 and Mercedes EQE start in the high $60,000s.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0181.statement: Reviewer cites 0-60 mph in 3.1 s for the standard AWD and a claimed 1.99 s for the 1,020-hp Plaid.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0182.statement: Reviewer finds the standard adaptive suspension controlled and comfortable for daily driving, though not as smooth as a Mercedes-Benz EQE.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0183.statement: Reviewer finds the handling lively when pushed, though less sporty than a Porsche Taycan.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0184.statement: Reviewer finds the standard yoke a bit awkward and notes a round wheel is available at no extra cost.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0185.statement: Reviewer praises the 17-inch screen's crisp graphics and fast responses and notes Netflix and Hulu streaming is supported.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0186.statement: Reviewer notes Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are not supported.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0187.statement: Reviewer highlights EPA ranges of 402 miles (AWD) and 348 miles (Plaid) and combined efficiency of 124 MPGe.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0188.statement: Reviewer praises the Supercharger network, noting charging to about 80% in as little as 30 minutes at a 250-kW charger.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0189.statement: Reviewer finds the cabin sparse and says it should be plusher, with better fit and finish for the price.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0190.statement: Reviewer notes rear legroom of 35.5 inches is only slightly more than the Model 3, though the car is wide.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0191.statement: Reviewer praises 25 cu ft of cargo space (61.4 cu ft with the seats folded), the 3.1 cu ft frunk and the wide opening.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0192.statement: Reviewer notes the fair purchase price is above MSRP and the 5-year cost to own is among the highest for high-end luxury cars, though resale values are above average.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0193.statement: Reviewer calls the reliability record patchy, citing panel gaps, paint flaws, loose weather strips and long service waits.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0232.statement: Reviewer (dual-motor Prestige) finds the power delivery linear and predictable.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0233.statement: Reviewer finds the ride on the adaptive air suspension composed and supple on all surfaces.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0234.statement: Reviewer finds the steering perfectly responsive and the car a pleasure to drive.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0235.statement: Reviewer welcomes the addition of one-pedal driving, which earlier Audi EVs lacked but most rivals offer.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0236.statement: Reviewer states the car (up to 392 mi single-motor, 377 mi dual-motor) beats its BMW and Mercedes rivals on range quite easily and comes close to the Model S's 402 miles.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0237.statement: Reviewer highlights the 800-volt system, which charges from 10% to 80% in 21 minutes on a DC fast charger.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0238.statement: Reviewer finds the optional front-passenger screen useful for changing navigation, and it cannot be seen from the driver's seat.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0239.statement: Reviewer notes the infotainment responds to more than 800 spoken commands.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0240.statement: Reviewer describes the interior as a pleasant mix of class and simplicity, with attention to textures.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0241.statement: Reviewer finds the 35.2 in of rear legroom acceptable; an average-size adult fits behind a driver of the same size.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0242.statement: Reviewer notes 26 cu ft of cargo space behind the rear seats versus 17.3 cu ft in the BMW i5, and 39.9 cu ft with the seats folded.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0243.statement: Reviewer finds the cabin quiet, with dual-pane front side windows on the top trim limiting wind noise.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0244.statement: Reviewer calls the optional Bang & Olufsen surround system, with headrest speakers, excellent.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0245.statement: Reviewer likes the large optional sunroof, which lets in light without heat and switches from clear to opaque at the touch of a button.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0246.statement: Reviewer calls the $67,195 starting price competitive and says the car may be a new class leader.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0255.statement: Reviewer notes the A6's 23 mpg combined rating trails the BMW 540i xDrive's 28 mpg.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0256.statement: Reviewer notes the BMW 5 Series and Mercedes E-Class have slightly larger trunks than the A6.

luis:us_tesla_audi-F0257.statement: Reviewer thinks the new A6 looks great inside, though Audi has caught up with interior design trends rather than led them.
